de.rule: Some verbs use de to link to what follows. Learn the verb and de together.
Adds a detail about ownership, contents, material or purpose, including an action: hora de partir = time to leave.

que.rule: Links what someone thinks, says, knows or hopes to a statement.
Means “than” when comparing people, things or situations.

se.formulaHTML: se + a possible situation + what happens then
se.rule: Means “if”: gives a possible situation and what happens then.
Can mean “oneself”, or belong with a verb such as sentir-se (feel). It does not always mean “oneself”.

o.rule: Means “the” before a masculine singular noun, such as livro (book).
Refers to “him” or a masculine “it”. These examples place o before the verb; other positions also occur.

nos.rule: Refers to us: someone sees or helps us, or tells us something.
Combines em + os: “in”, “on” or “at the”, before a masculine plural noun.

naquele.rule: Combines em + aquele: “in”, “on” or “at that”. It can refer to places, things or times.

um.rule: Means “a / an”. Use the form that matches the noun’s gender and number.

uma.rule: Means “a / an”. Use the form that matches the noun’s gender and number.

eu.rule: Means “I”. Names who does the action; the pronoun can often be left out.

ela.rule: Means “she / it”. Names who does the action; the pronoun can often be left out.
